questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a different country and culture to my own, exciting courses, and experiencing another study environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid I did not feel I got the full study abroad experience. My classes were online and I didn't get to interact much with my fellow students. The best parts of my stay were exploring the country and Scottish nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The Stirling University website offered much information, but any queries I had were quickly and easily answered by the study abroad team at Stirling.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study abroad team emailed much useful information regularly during my stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The website made it easy to see which options of accommodation I had and how to apply through the portal.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice to live in town so you're close to shopping, pubs, restaurants etc. You do need to get on the bus to go to campus which needs a little planning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I chose the cheapest option, which was still quite expensive, and the showers were awful and we had to buy everything for the kitchen ourselves, which was quite disappointing. I heard that the more expensive options were the same.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found courses in the course catalogue and then I had to send my choices and reserve choices with my acceptance form, and then I would be told which of the courses I could and could not register for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email the study abroad team and the course catalogue had most information I needed when choosing courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could not register for all of my choices due to different reasons, but I was successful in registering for some of my first choices and some reserves.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Watch out for credits, Autumn/Spring semester, if you need to have taken another class before taking the one you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found some of my classes to be challenging and others to be a bit below the level that I am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is much fewer weekly teaching seminars and much more independent study at Stirling with only 1 hour per class per week compared to 3-6 hours per class per week at UCPH. However, the teachers at Stirling give much more personal and detailed feedback for assignments and offer more obvious help with academic issues.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FMSU9AS - Gender and Representation
LINU911 - Language and Society
JOUU9X1 - Introduction to Journalism Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
FMSU9AS - Gender and Representation
This course was by far the most challenging and exciting of my courses. The teacher, Darren, has my full praise, he did a great job and many interesting topics were discussed during the course that enlightened me not only academically but also personally.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Basic groceries, coffee at coffee shops and drinks at pubs were quite cheap. National train tickets were a bit expensive. Rent for the housing was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I used the gym and the swimming pool and one yoga class. There were many opportunities. I didn't join any clubs but there were several.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We went on a highland trip with a private company that the university collaborated with to get us a good deal.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The highland trip, definitely. It was an amazing way to see loads of the Scottish highlands and nature in only three days and quite cheap compared to how much you get. The gym facilities are great, so I recommend those to anyone who wants to exercise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Highland trip, go on hikes (remember proper footwear), Loch Ness/Inverness, visit Glasgow and Edinburgh, cinema, The Settle Inn (oldest pub in Stirling), Stirling Castle, Wallace Monument, take the train to Aberdeen and get an amazing view of the coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local community in Stirling is very nice and polite. It was quite easy to interact with people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Because of covid I didn't socialise a whole lot, but go to parties, or "gaffs" as they're called, if there are any in your accommodation area.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people always interact with you, say hiya when you enter a shop and see you when you leave, sorry if they bump into you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get the First Bus app and use the University of Stirling tickets for a discount, get to campus early if you want a study space, explore the paths on campus, they are great for a long walk.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Scottish nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting other students due to covid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
